page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-32GB is a general-purpose virtual machine within UpCloud's Cloud Native series, powered by the KVM hypervisor. The instance is provisioned with 8 vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz, configured across 8 physical cores with 1 thread per core using a shared allocation model. Cache architecture includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. It comes equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM balance (4.0 GB per core). Local storage is not bundled, no dedicated GPUs are present, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a split compute profile influenced by the shared-core scheduling. Single-core performance shows divergence, registering a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2,352.0 alongside a high text-processing score of 2,875.0, but showing bottom-decile results in stress-ng single-core tests (788.49). Multi-core benchmarks sit consistently in the average range, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,375.0, a PassMark CPU score of 15,377.49, and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 72.47 GB/sec. Instruction support covers AVX, AES-NI, and SHA-NI, while lacking AVX-512 and AMX extensions.

Memory and application-level workloads present specific throughput constraints. Large-block uncached memory write throughput measures 25.08 GB/sec and the PassMark memory score is 1,303.4, both scoring in the bottom quartile. Despite this, cached small-block read bandwidth peaks at 806.66 GB/sec, and Redis SET throughput reaches an average 11.19 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput settles in the lower tier at 3.71 GB/sec. Large language model inference capabilities demonstrate workable speeds for lightweight 135M parameter models (741.97 prompt tokens/sec), but show clear latency degradation on 7B models (6.57 generation tokens/sec).

Given its balanced core-to-RAM allocation and shared-core cost profile, the CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-32GB provides solid resource efficiency for multi-threaded background processing, CI/CD code compilation (15,036.0 in Clang tests), caching layers, and intermediate database operations. Tradeoffs include the absence of included local storage, shared CPU resource contention risks, and weaker raw memory write throughput.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-32GB is a general-purpose cloud instance delivering 8 shared vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 7542 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 32.0 GB of RAM. Operating under the KVM hypervisor on an x86_64 architecture, it provisions a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It lacks integrated local storage, contains no GPU accelerators, and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Synthetic performance benchmarks reflect steady mid-range multi-core output, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,375.0 and PassMark CPU score of 15,377.49, complemented by strong Geekbench single-core text execution. However, large-block memory write throughput and static web serving benchmark in lower performance quartiles. The configuration is cost-effective for multi-threaded applications, software compilation pipelines, lightweight caching systems, and general container workloads that do not mandate dedicated core occupancy or sustained high memory write speeds.
